patients.summary: Operations manager with long-standing hypertension who joins the practice in 2017; ADPKD found in 2020, then psychogenic ED, an adjustment disorder, aortic regurgitation with an ascending aneurysm, flutter-driven cardiomyopathy that recovers after ablation, stage III follicular lymphoma treated to remission, and an aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage in March 2026.

documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is looking for a new primary care doctor; his previous office is reducing hours and he wants somewhere he can reach the doctor directly. Explained membership and how insurance still applies for labs and specialists. Has high blood pressure, on two pills. Booked new patient physical 6/21 at 8:00. Release form emailed so we can request his old records.

documents.title: New Patient Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
42M establishing care. Previous PCP office cutting back, wants more access.

HTN: told about 5 yrs ago after a run of high readings at a work health fair. On lisinopril 20 and HCTZ 25 for several years, takes them in the morning, rarely misses. Doesn't check at home. No HA, CP, SOB, edema.

PMH: HTN. No surgeries. No hospitalizations.
Meds: lisinopril 20 mg daily, HCTZ 25 mg daily. No supplements.
All: NKDA.
FH: father had kidney disease and eventually a kidney transplant, pt not sure of the details. Paternal grandfather died at 58 of bleeding in the brain. Mother: HTN, high cholesterol.
SH: married. Senior operations manager at a manufacturing/distribution company, there about 10 yrs, long days. Never smoker. Alcohol 2-3 drinks a week, social. No drugs. Walks some on weekends.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: BP 138/88 (repeat similar), HR 70, SpO2 98%. Ht 180 cm, wt 88 kg.
Well appearing. HEENT unremarkable, fundi not visualized well without dilation. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses felt. Ext without edema. Skin no worrisome lesions. Neuro grossly normal.

A/P
1. HTN - borderline on two drugs. Ask him to buy a home cuff and send readings. Continue lisinopril/HCTZ. CMP.
2. Health maintenance - CBC, CMP, lipids, UA, hep C screen (never done). Tdap - doesn't remember last one, will check old records. Flu in the fall.
3. Records release signed.

RTC 6 months for BP, sooner with readings.

documents.title: Visit summary
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Today: new patient physical. Your blood pressure was 138/88; goal is under 130/80. Please buy an upper-arm home cuff and send two weeks of morning readings through the portal. Keep taking lisinopril 20 mg and hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg each morning. Blood and urine tests were sent; results in a few days.

documents.title: Results from your physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Glenn, labs look good overall. Kidney function, potassium and blood counts are normal and the hepatitis C screen is negative. Your triglycerides are high and LDL is borderline; less alcohol, fewer refined carbs and more walking would help both. We'll recheck in a year. Send me some home blood pressure readings when you have the cuff.

documents.title: Flank pain
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
45M. About six months of on-and-off aching in both flanks, sometimes one side more than the other, lasts hours to a day, no clear trigger. Thought it was his back from long drives between sites. No dysuria, no visible blood in urine, no fever, no stones in the past. Over the last few weeks also headaches, a few a week, frontal pressure, gone with rest or sleep. No vision change, no weakness.
Reminded me his father had a kidney transplant; still doesn't know what the disease was.
Meds lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25.

Exam: BP 160/88, rechecked 154/90. Afebrile. Abdomen soft; fullness in both flanks on deep palpation, mild tenderness, no CVA tenderness to percussion. Neuro nonfocal. Fundi grossly ok.

A/P
1. Bilateral flank pain with flank fullness and a father with kidney failure: renal ultrasound, BMP, UA today.
2. Headaches - tension pattern by description; BP is up too. Avoid NSAIDs for now.
3. HTN above goal. Will revisit once the kidney picture is clear.

documents.title: Lab call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt: creatinine 1.8, BUN 29 - well above his old 1.0-1.1. UA clean, no protein or blood. Asked him to avoid NSAIDs. Ultrasound booked for 2/20; will decide on nephrology with that result. He's understandably worried, answered questions.

reports.text:
Indication: bilateral flank pain, rising creatinine, family history of kidney disease.
Technique: grayscale and color Doppler imaging of both kidneys and the bladder.
Right kidney: 15.8 cm in length, enlarged. Multiple simple-appearing cysts of varying sizes throughout the cortex and medulla, the largest in the lower pole. No hydronephrosis. No shadowing calculi.
Left kidney: 16.4 cm in length, enlarged. Multiple cysts of varying sizes replacing much of the parenchyma. No hydronephrosis. No shadowing calculi.
Bladder: partially distended, unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Bilaterally enlarged kidneys with multiple bilateral cysts of varying size, in keeping with polycystic kidney disease. No hydronephrosis or stones.

documents.title: Ultrasound result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Discussed ultrasound: both kidneys enlarged with many cysts, pattern of polycystic kidney disease; likely explains the flank pain and probably what his father had. Referring to nephrology for diagnosis and plan; staff to push for an early slot. He'll ask his father's side about the diagnosis.

documents.title: Referral to nephrology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Referral: Nephrology. 45M with HTN on lisinopril 20/HCTZ 25, six months of bilateral flank pain, recent headaches. Creatinine 1.8, BUN 29 (2/11/20), prior creatinine 1.0-1.15. UA negative for protein and blood. Renal US 2/20/20: bilaterally enlarged kidneys with multiple cysts. Father had kidney failure with transplant, diagnosis unknown to patient. Question polycystic kidney disease; please evaluate and advise. NKDA.

documents.title: Nephrology consultation
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outside Nephrology Group - Consultation
Date of service: 03/18/2020
Re: Glenn Cabral, DOB 08/31/1974
Referred by primary care for bilateral renal cysts.

Thank you for sending Mr. Cabral, a 45-year-old man, seen for half a year of intermittent bilateral flank discomfort and headaches that started more recently. He has had hypertension for several years, treated with lisinopril 20 mg daily and hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily. No known drug allergies. He believes his father had a kidney transplant but cannot say what the underlying disease was. Never smoker, drinks socially, works as a senior operations manager.

Exam: BP 155/95. Both flanks have palpable masses consistent with enlarged kidneys. Remainder of the exam is unremarkable.

Data reviewed: creatinine 1.8 mg/dL and BUN 29 mg/dL (02/11/2020), urinalysis without protein or blood. Renal ultrasound 02/20/2020 with multiple bilateral cysts of varying sizes in both enlarged kidneys.

Impression: autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease, with hypertension above target. The creatinine of 1.8 sits higher than I would expect from these images and his prior values, so I would like it repeated in about six weeks before we stage his kidney function.

Recommendations:
1. Repeat BMP in roughly 6 weeks; please forward.
2. Blood pressure target below 130/80; continue lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide for now.
3. Generous fluid intake, limit NSAIDs.
4. Return to nephrology in about a year.

Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Kidney doctor
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Saw the kidney doctor last week, he says it's polycystic kidney disease. Probably what my dad has too. He wants another blood test in a few weeks - can I do it at your office with everything going on with covid?

documents.title: RE: Kidney doctor
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Glenn, yes, our lab is open with distancing. The order is in; early May is perfect. Please wear a mask and come straight to the lab door.

documents.title: Repeat kidney function
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Creatinine 1.2, much better than February. Forwarded to nephrology. Glenn, this is reassuring - continue your current medicines and keep fluids up.

documents.title: HTN follow-up / research study question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Masked visit. In for BP and to ask about joining a new hypertension study he saw advertised for people with kidney disease; wants to know whether it's worth doing.

Flank aches less frequent since spring. Headaches occasional. Taking lisinopril 20 and HCTZ 25 daily.

Family history now clarified with his family: father has autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease, reached end-stage kidney disease at 62 and later had a transplant. Paternal grandfather died at 58 of a ruptured brain aneurysm. Mother: hypertension and high cholesterol.

Exam: BP 146/92, repeat 144/90. HR 72. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Flanks full bilaterally, nontender. No edema.

A/P
1. Hypertension with ADPKD, above the nephrology target. Continue lisinopril/HCTZ; home log for 2 weeks.
2. Research study: went through what joining would mean - eligibility screening, possible randomization, extra visits and labs, he can stop at any time, and his usual care continues regardless. Gave him the study coordinator's contact sheet. He'll read it and decide.
3. ADPKD - nephrology yearly; creatinine 1.2 in May.
4. Flu vaccine today.
RTC 6 mo.

documents.title: Urology consultation
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Outside urology group - New Patient Consultation
Visit 09/16/2021

HPI: 47-year-old man with ADPKD and hypertension, followed by nephrology and by his internist for blood pressure, referred for erectile difficulty. For about six months he has had trouble sustaining erections. He describes this as a real strain on his marriage. Desire is unchanged. On direct questioning he still gets erections during sleep and sometimes on waking.

Medications: lisinopril 20 mg daily. Allergies: none known.
Social: nonsmoker, social alcohol.

Exam: genitourinary and general examination unremarkable.

Labs reviewed from primary care (08/03/2021): fasting glucose 96, total cholesterol 190, HDL 45, LDL 120, triglycerides 250, total testosterone 550.

Assessment: erectile dysfunction, psychogenic. Preserved nocturnal and morning erections, intact libido, normal testosterone and glucose, and a clear relationship stressor point away from a vascular or hormonal cause.

Plan: recommended counseling with a sex therapist or couples counselor; list of local therapists provided. No medication started today. Follow up with us as needed.

orders.reason: headaches and poor concentration after a major work stressor

documents.title: Headaches, poor focus
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Last appt of the day. About 6 wks of a dull, all-over headache most days, builds through the afternoon, worst by evening. No nausea or vomiting, no light or sound sensitivity, no waking from sleep, no worst-ever headache, no neuro symptoms. Also can't concentrate, rereads emails.
Started right after his company announced layoffs and a restructuring. He's been running the restructuring plan for his division, 12-hr days, says he hasn't had time to think about what it means for him. Sleep 5-6 hrs. Alcohol unchanged.
Meds lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25.

Exam: BP 141/96, HR 70. Tense but appropriate. Neck supple, mild trapezius tightness. Cranial nerves intact, strength and reflexes symmetric, gait normal. Fundi: discs flat as far as I can see.
PHQ-9 9, GAD-7 8.

A/P
1. Daily headache with poor concentration in the setting of a big work stressor; nonfocal exam. CBC, CMP, TSH to be thorough. Referral to psychiatry for evaluation and therapy options - he's open to it.
2. HTN a bit high today, likely stress; continue meds.
3. RTC 2-3 months.

documents.title: Referral to psychiatry
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Referral: Psychiatry / Behavioral Health. 47M with ADPKD and HTN, six weeks of daily headaches and poor concentration that began with layoff news at work. Nonfocal neuro exam. PHQ-9 9, GAD-7 8, no SI. CBC, CMP, TSH pending. Requesting evaluation and therapy options.

documents.title: Blood work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glenn, blood counts, metabolic panel (including kidney function) and thyroid are all normal. Psychiatry should call this week; let me know if they don't.

documents.title: Psychiatric evaluation
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Outpatient Behavioral Health - Initial Psychiatric Evaluation
Date of service: 03/15/2022

Reason for referral: two months of headaches and poor concentration.

History: 47-year-old married man with ADPKD and hypertension. Daily, dull, diffuse headaches that worsen toward evening; denies nausea, vomiting, photophobia and phonophobia. Difficulty concentrating at work. Onset closely followed the announcement of layoffs at the company where he has worked for 15 years. Since then he has thrown himself into preparing his division for the restructuring and admits he has not stopped to consider what it means for him personally. No prior psychiatric history, no suicidal thoughts, no substance use beyond social alcohol.

Medications: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily (lisinopril per patient). NKDA.

Vitals: BP 145/90, HR 78. Neurological screen without focal findings; remainder unremarkable.
Labs reviewed: CBC, CMP and TSH normal (02/2022).

Mental status: well groomed, cooperative, mildly anxious affect, linear thought process, no psychosis, insight fair.

Diagnosis: adjustment disorder, in response to an occupational stressor.

Plan: weekly individual psychotherapy (CBT-based) with one of our therapists for about 8-10 sessions, focusing on stress and sleep. No medication indicated at this time. Re-evaluate in 2 months.

documents.title: Psychiatry follow-up
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body: Follow-up 05/24/2022. Has attended 8 therapy sessions. Headaches now a couple of times a week and milder; concentration improved; sleeping closer to 7 hours. Mood euthymic. Adjustment disorder improving. Will finish the therapy block and follow up with us as needed. No medications from this office.

orders.reason: exertional dyspnea, wide pulse pressure, murmur

documents.title: Dyspnea
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
First visit in about a year; missed his BP follow-ups through the restructuring. Comes in because over the past few months he's been more winded - stairs at work, carrying groceries - and can't keep up on the weekend walks. Also notices his heart pounding in his chest when he lies on his left side at night. No chest pain, no fainting, no leg swelling, no orthopnea.
Stress better; finished therapy last spring, headaches mostly gone.
Meds lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25 - admits some missed doses.

Exam: BP 149/52 (repeated, similar), HR 76 regular. SpO2 normal. Bounding radial pulses. Diastolic murmur along the left sternal border, heard best sitting forward. Lungs clear. No JVD, no edema.
ECG: sinus, normal.

A/P
1. Exertional dyspnea with a wide pulse pressure and a diastolic murmur: concern for aortic valve leak. Referred to cardiology, asked for a prompt appointment; they'll do the echo.
2. HTN, systolic high. Take the meds every day; we'll adjust once cardiology weighs in.
3. Adjustment disorder - resolved.
4. Overdue labs/physical: will do after cardiology.
RTC after cardiology.

documents.title: Referral to cardiology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Referral: Cardiology, please see within 2-3 weeks. 48M with HTN and ADPKD. Months of exertional dyspnea, pounding heartbeat lying on the left side. BP 149/52, bounding pulses, diastolic murmur at LSB. ECG sinus, normal. Question aortic regurgitation; echo requested. Meds lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25. NKDA.

events.reason: progressive shortness of breath, reduced exercise tolerance

reports.text: Left ventricle mildly dilated with normal wall thickness. LVEF 55% by biplane method, no regional wall motion abnormality. Normal diastolic filling for age. Right ventricle normal in size and function. Trileaflet aortic valve with moderate aortic regurgitation; no aortic stenosis. Mitral, tricuspid and pulmonic valves without significant abnormality. Ascending aorta aneurysmally dilated; aortic root normal. No pericardial effusion. Estimated RV systolic pressure normal.
reports.conclusion: Moderate aortic regurgitation. Aneurysm of the ascending aorta. Mildly dilated left ventricle with LVEF 55%.

reports.text: PA and lateral views. The cardiac silhouette is enlarged. Lungs are clear. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax. No pulmonary edema. Bones unremarkable.

documents.title: Cardiology consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group - Consultation
Date of visit: 03/27/2023

Reason: worsening breathlessness and exercise intolerance.

HPI: 48-year-old man with ADPKD and hypertension, followed by nephrology and primary care, with a few months of progressive dyspnea and reduced exercise tolerance and a pounding sensation in the chest, most noticeable lying on his left side. By his account his blood pressure has not been looked after for about a year and he has missed doses; it has been poorly controlled.

Medications: lisinopril 20 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: father ADPKD with ESRD at 62; paternal grandfather died at 58 of a ruptured cerebral aneurysm; mother hypertension, hyperlipidemia.
Social: never smoker, 2-3 drinks/week, senior operations manager.

Exam: BP 150/50. Bounding peripheral pulses with a brisk carotid upstroke; nail-bed pulsations visible with light pressure on the nail tip. Diastolic murmur at the left sternal border. No peripheral edema. Lungs clear.

Studies today:
- Echo: moderate aortic regurgitation, trileaflet valve; aneurysm of the ascending aorta; LV mildly dilated, EF 55%.
- CXR: enlarged cardiac silhouette, clear lung fields.

Assessment:
1. Aortic regurgitation, moderate, with preserved LV function.
2. Ascending aortic aneurysm - needs exact sizing.
3. Hypertension, poorly controlled.

Plan: CT angiography of the chest to measure the aorta; I will see him back after it. Strict BP control and daily adherence; we discussed avoiding heavy straining/lifting. Will send recommendations to primary care.

reports.text:
CT angiography of the chest with IV contrast, ECG-gated.
Aortic root at the sinuses normal. The ascending aorta measures 4.5 cm in maximal diameter, measured perpendicular to the vessel centerline at the level of the right pulmonary artery. No dissection flap, no intramural hematoma. Aortic arch and descending thoracic aorta normal in caliber. Pulmonary arteries normal. Heart enlarged; no pericardial effusion. Lungs clear. No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy. Visualized upper abdomen: partially imaged upper poles of both kidneys contain cysts, consistent with known polycystic kidney disease.
reports.conclusion: Ascending aortic aneurysm, 4.5 cm. No dissection. Arch and descending aorta normal caliber.

documents.title: CT angiogram reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: CT angiography reviewed: ascending aorta 4.5 cm, no dissection. Cardiology to follow up. BP control is key - he has a visit with us next month.

documents.title: Cardiology follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Cardiology follow-up 05/03/2023.
CT angiography: ascending aorta 4.5 cm without dissection; arch and descending aorta normal.
Symptoms unchanged, mild. Meds: lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25 (reports taking daily now).
Impression: moderate aortic regurgitation with preserved EF; 4.5 cm ascending aortic aneurysm, below a surgical threshold.
Plan: surveillance echo and aortic imaging in 12 months, sooner for symptoms. Blood pressure control is the main lever; we would appreciate primary care's help getting him under 130/80. Return in a year.

Electrophysiology Laboratory - Procedure Report
Date: 10/24/2023
Procedure: electrophysiology study and radiofrequency ablation of the cavotricuspid isthmus.
Indication: typical atrial flutter with tachycardia-mediated LV dysfunction; on apixaban uninterrupted for over 4 weeks.
Access: right femoral vein, ultrasound guided.
Findings: patient in atrial flutter on arrival, cycle length consistent with typical counterclockwise flutter, confirmed isthmus-dependent by entrainment. Linear ablation across the isthmus terminated flutter to sinus rhythm; bidirectional block confirmed. No other arrhythmia inducible.
Complications: none. Hemostasis with a figure-of-eight stitch.
Plan: continue apixaban for at least 3 months, continue metoprolol, repeat echocardiogram in about 3 months. Same-day discharge.

Assessment: isolated supraclavicular adenopathy with elevated LDH; lymphoma is the leading concern.

Plan: excisional biopsy of the node (surgical oncology next week). If lymphoma is confirmed, PET/CT for staging. Will update primary care.

events.reason: excisional biopsy, left supraclavicular lymph node

reports.text:
Specimen: left supraclavicular lymph node, excision.
Gross: a 3.1 x 2.6 x 2.0 cm tan-pink lymph node.
Microscopic: nodal architecture effaced by closely packed neoplastic follicles composed of centrocytes with 6 to 15 centroblasts per high-power field. No diffuse large-cell areas identified.
Immunohistochemistry: neoplastic cells positive for CD20, CD10, BCL2 and BCL6; CD5 negative. Ki-67 approximately 20%.
Flow cytometry: CD10-positive monoclonal B-cell population, lambda light chain restricted.
reports.conclusion: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma: follicular lymphoma, grade 2 (WHO grade 1-2), left supraclavicular lymph node.

reports.conclusion: FDG-avid lymphoma above and below the diaphragm: left supraclavicular, para-aortic and bilateral common iliac nodes. No organ or marrow involvement. Findings positive for distant disease.

documents.title: Oncology treatment plan
documents.author: hematology/oncology
documents.body:
Hematology/Oncology follow-up 04/16/2024.
Pathology: follicular lymphoma, grade 2. PET/CT 04/09: FDG-avid disease in the left supraclavicular region and in para-aortic and bilateral common iliac nodes; no extranodal or marrow involvement. Stage III.
He remains fatigued; no B symptoms. LDH elevated at diagnosis. Hepatitis B surface antigen and core antibody negative.
Assessment: stage III follicular lymphoma, grade 2, symptomatic, with elevated LDH - treatment indicated.
Plan: bendamustine and rituximab every 28 days for 6 cycles, starting 04/30. Chose a regimen without an anthracycline given his recent cardiomyopathy. Counts and chemistry with each cycle. Avoid live vaccines during and after therapy; inactivated flu and COVID vaccines are fine. End-of-treatment PET after cycle 6.
Discussed goals: high likelihood of a long remission. He and his wife asked good questions.

Regional tertiary center, Neurosciences ICU / Neurosurgery - Discharge Summary
Admitted 03/14/2026 (transfer from community ED); discharged 03/26/2026.

Diagnosis: aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage from a ruptured 7 mm anterior communicating artery aneurysm, treated with endovascular coiling 03/15/2026.

Course: arrived alert, no focal deficits. CT angiography showed the aneurysm; coiled the next morning. Nimodipine started on admission. Blood pressure controlled with IV agents then his home lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide. Daily transcranial Dopplers and neuro checks without clinically significant vasospasm; no hydrocephalus, no drain needed. Sodium stayed normal. Headache gradually improved. Ambulating independently; neurologically intact at discharge.

Discharge medications:
- nimodipine 60 mg by mouth every 4 hours to complete 21 days (last dose 04/04/2026)
- lisinopril 20 mg daily
- hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily
- acetaminophen as needed for headache

Instructions: no driving or heavy lifting until reviewed in neurosurgery clinic. Blood pressure goal under 140/90 at first, ideally lower long term - primary care to follow. Neurosurgery clinic in 6-8 weeks; follow-up angiogram at 6 months. Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Home from the hospital
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt's wife called: Glenn home since yesterday after 12 days at the tertiary center for a brain bleed from an aneurysm, coiled. Headache 3/10, taking nimodipine every 4 hours on an alarm, BP at home 140s/90. No new weakness, speech fine. Booked with PCP Tue 3/31. Asked them to bring discharge papers; records requested from the hospital.

events.reason: follow-up after hospitalization for subarachnoid hemorrhage

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Discharge summary and angiography report received yesterday and reviewed.

SAH 3/14 from a ruptured 7 mm AComm aneurysm, coiled 3/15, 12 days in the neuro-ICU/floor without vasospasm or hydrocephalus. Home 3/26.
Now: headache 2-3/10, dull, much better each day. Mild fatigue. No weakness, numbness, vision or speech problems. Nimodipine q4h through 4/4 - tolerating, a bit lightheaded at times. Not driving; wife driving.
Meds: nimodipine 60 q4h (short course), lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25, acetaminophen prn. NKDA.

Exam: BP 146/88, repeat 144/86, HR 74. Alert, oriented, conversant, normal speech. Cranial nerves intact, strength 5/5 throughout, gait steady. Groin site clean. Diastolic murmur LSB, regular. Lungs clear.

A/P
1. Aneurysmal SAH s/p coiling - recovering well. Neurosurgery clinic in May, follow-up angiogram ~September.
2. HTN - above goal after the bleed and with his aorta. Adding amlodipine 5 mg daily now; will watch for lightheadedness while nimodipine overlaps (ends 4/4) - he'll sit/stand slowly. Home BP twice daily, send in 2 wks. Goal under 130/80.
3. ADPKD - BMP today.
4. Lymphoma surveillance in April, cardiology echo due.
RTC 2 mo, sooner prn.

documents.title: Visit summary
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: New medicine: amlodipine 5 mg once daily. Finish nimodipine as prescribed through 4/4. Check your blood pressure morning and evening and send readings in 2 weeks; goal under 130/80. Stand up slowly. Call 911 for a sudden severe headache, weakness, numbness, trouble speaking or confusion.

documents.title: Labs from Tuesday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sodium, potassium and kidney function all fine. Start the amlodipine as planned and send home readings in two weeks.

documents.title: BP log
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Done with the nimodipine 4/4. Two weeks on amlodipine: mornings 126-134 / 74-80, evenings a little lower. No more lightheadedness. Headaches only occasional now.

documents.title: RE: BP log
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Those are good numbers, Glenn - right where we want them. Stay on all three. See you in June.

documents.title: Lymphoma surveillance
documents.author: hematology/oncology
documents.body: Surveillance 04/21/2026, 19 months after BR. Interval subarachnoid hemorrhage 03/2026, coiled, recovering. No B symptoms; fatigue attributed to recent hospitalization. No adenopathy or splenomegaly. CBC normal, LDH 199. Complete remission continues. Next visit in 6 months, then yearly.

events.reason: follow-up after coiled anterior communicating artery aneurysm

documents.title: Neurosurgery clinic follow-up
documents.author: neurosurgery
documents.body:
Neurosurgery clinic, 05/12/2026.
Seven weeks after aneurysmal SAH from a 7 mm AComm aneurysm treated with coiling. Recovering well. Mild headaches a few times a week, relieved by acetaminophen, and some end-of-day fatigue. No focal symptoms. Back to work part-time from home. BP well controlled on lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide and amlodipine added by his PCP.
Exam: neurologically intact.
Plan: cleared to drive and return to usual activity, avoiding heavy straining for another month. Follow-up catheter angiogram planned for September 2026 to assess the coil mass. Continue strict BP control. NKDA.

events.reason: follow-up: blood pressure, recovery after subarachnoid hemorrhage

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
About 12 weeks after SAH/coiling. Neurosurgery cleared him to drive in May. Headaches down to once a week, mild. Energy improving, back in the office three days a week. Mood ok, PHQ-2 1. Home BP 120s-130/70s.
Meds: amlodipine 5, lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25, acetaminophen prn. NKDA.

Exam: BP 128/76, HR 68. Neuro nonfocal. Diastolic murmur LSB, regular. Lungs clear. Ankles without edema on amlodipine.

A/P
1. HTN - at goal on three drugs. Continue. BMP today.
2. SAH s/p coiling - follow-up angiogram in September per neurosurgery.
3. AR/ascending aneurysm - cardiology echo this summer.
4. Follicular lymphoma - in remission, oncology October.
5. ADPKD - nephrology November.
RTC September.

documents.title: Visit summary
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Blood pressure 128/76 - at goal. Keep taking amlodipine 5 mg, lisinopril 20 mg and hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily. Blood test today; we'll message results. Next visit in September.

documents.title: June labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Potassium and sodium normal on the three blood pressure medicines; creatinine 1.35, about where it was at nephrology last fall.

events.reason: surveillance of aortic regurgitation and ascending aortic aneurysm

reports.text: Left ventricle normal in size, LVEF 55-60%. Normal RV. Trileaflet aortic valve with moderate aortic regurgitation, unchanged. Ascending aorta 4.6 cm, unchanged from 03/2025. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Stable moderate aortic regurgitation with normal LV size and function. Ascending aorta 4.6 cm, unchanged.

documents.title: Cardiology surveillance
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Cardiology, 07/21/2026.
Interval aneurysmal SAH in March, coiled; recovering. No cardiac symptoms.
Meds: amlodipine 5, lisinopril 20, hydrochlorothiazide 25. NKDA.
BP 131/74. Echo: moderate AR, normal LV, EF 55-60%; ascending aorta 4.6 cm, unchanged.
Impression: stable moderate AR and ascending aortic aneurysm.
Plan: continue current regimen; repeat echo in 12 months.

documents.title: Cardiology note filed
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Cardiology visit note and echo report 7/21/2026 received by fax, scanned and routed to PCP.

documents.title: Cardiology note reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Cardiology 7/21 reviewed: AR moderate and aorta 4.6 cm, both stable. Nothing new for us. Will discuss at September visit.

documents.title: Refill: amlodipine, lisinopril, HCTZ
documents.author: MA
documents.body: 90-day supplies of amlodipine 5 mg, lisinopril 20 mg and HCTZ 25 mg sent. Seen 6/8, BMP 6/8 normal. Next visit 9/15.

documents.title: Angiogram
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Neurosurgery scheduled my follow-up angiogram for September 22. Do I need to stop any of my BP pills beforehand, or is that their call?

documents.title: RE: Angiogram
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Glenn - the angiography team will give you the instructions; usually blood pressure medicines are taken as normal with a sip of water. Please confirm with them at the pre-procedure call. We'll see you on 9/15.
